newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: ASSET SWAP UPS MONDAY S.AFRICA SHARE TRADE - DEALERS.
newsitem.headline: ASSET SWAP UPS MONDAY S.AFRICA SHARE TRADE - DEALERS.

text.p: A cluster of blue-chip South African shares saw heavy trade early on Monday on the back of a possible asset swap worth around 140 million rand, dealers said.

They said the large volumes, evident in stocks including key iron and steel producer Iscor , foods group Del Monte (Delfood) and tyre manufacturer BTR Dunlop , had taken place in overnight deals on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange carried out by brokerage Deutsche Morgan Grenfell.
"When you see a big block of trades overnight, and if it was done by the same broker, it suggests that it was an asset swap," one share dealer said.
"It's difficult to peg the size but when you add all the large deals by the broker together its around 140 million (rand)," he added.
Another dealer said the deals could also have been basket trades linked to futures-driven arbitrage business.

By 0930 GMT Iscor had traded nearly 6.3 million shares to 312 cents, a fall of two cents. Delfood was unchanged at 300 cents after over 1.5 million stocks traded, while BTR added five cents to 485 cents in volume of 1.46 million.

Dealers said other stocks which also looked to be involved in the block included chemical stocks Hoechst South Africa which traded 1.1 million stocks and AECI with 152,000. Impala Platinum was also suggested with over 370,000 stocks traded.

South African companies' offshore investment activities are curbed by foreign exchange control regulations. Institutions are, however, allowed to invest up to 10 percent of each individual mutual fund abroad through "swapping" investments with an overseas concern.
South Africa's biggest investment group, Old Mutual, said last month it was concluding a new asset swap programme.
